sections.markdown:
# AI Agent Optimization — a measurable before/after

**ISI-6720 · Phase 5** · Tenant `oat05854.dev.apps.dynatracelabs.com` · data: `gen_ai.*` spans from the kagent crew (`workshop.attendee == "${WORKSHOP_PREFIX}" and service.namespace == "kagent"`).

This notebook is the *reproducible story* behind module **`docs/06-optimize.md`**. It follows the optimization loop:

> **observe → find the waste → make one change → re-measure → keep only if quality held.**

Run it top-to-bottom. Sections 1–3 find the waste; section 4 is the change; section 5 is the measured before/after; section 6 is the keep/revert rule.

## 1 · Rank agents by spend
Start at the top of this list — a 20% cut on the priciest agent beats a 50% cut on a rare one.

input.value:
fetch spans
| filter workshop.attendee == "${WORKSHOP_PREFIX}" and service.namespace == "kagent" and isNotNull(gen_ai.usage.output_tokens)
| summarize llmCalls = count(),
    inputTokens = sum(gen_ai.usage.input_tokens),
    outputTokens = sum(gen_ai.usage.output_tokens),
    by:{agent = service.name}
| fieldsAdd totalTokens = inputTokens + outputTokens
| sort totalTokens desc

sections.markdown:
## 2 · Spot the waste signature
A high **input : output ratio** and a large **avg input per call** means the model re-reads a bloated context (big system prompt + unused tool schemas) on every single call. `${WORKSHOP_PREFIX}-sre-agent` is the outlier here.

input.value:
fetch spans
| filter workshop.attendee == "${WORKSHOP_PREFIX}" and service.namespace == "kagent" and isNotNull(gen_ai.usage.output_tokens)
| summarize llmCalls = count(),
    inputTokens = sum(gen_ai.usage.input_tokens),
    outputTokens = sum(gen_ai.usage.output_tokens),
    by:{agent = service.name}
| fieldsAdd totalTokens = inputTokens + outputTokens,
    inOutRatio = round(toDouble(inputTokens) / outputTokens, decimals: 1),
    avgInputPerCall = round(toDouble(inputTokens) / llmCalls)
| sort avgInputPerCall desc

sections.title: Input : output ratio & avg input per call

sections.markdown:
## 3 · Which tools does the agent actually use?
Every tool granted in the agent's `toolNames` is described in **every** prompt — billed as input tokens whether it is called or not. List the tools the SRE agent *actually* calls, then compare against its granted set in `agents/sre/sre-agent.yaml`. Anything granted-but-never-called is pure overhead to drop.

input.value:
fetch spans
| filter workshop.attendee == "${WORKSHOP_PREFIX}" and service.namespace == "kagent"
    and gen_ai.operation.name == "execute_tool" and gen_ai.tool.name != "(merged tools)"
| summarize calls = count(), by:{agent = service.name, tool = gen_ai.tool.name}
| sort agent asc, calls desc

sections.markdown:
### 3a · Tool coverage — the NEVER-called tools, by name
The cell above lists tools the agent *did* call. The optimization you want is the **complement**: which granted tools did it **never** call? Those are the pure-overhead schemas to drop first. The cell below left-joins the SRE agent's **granted** tool set (from `agents/sre/sre-agent.yaml`, shipped as `tool-grants.lookup.json`) against the tools it actually called — `coalesce(…, 0)` turns an uncalled tool into `0` and the `verdict` column flags the drop candidates. The `service.name` filter is **intentional** here: coverage is a per-agent question. Swap the `service.name` and the inline `data record(…)` rows to score another agent.

input.value:
data record(tool = "k8s_get_resources"),
     record(tool = "k8s_describe_resource"),
     record(tool = "k8s_get_resource_yaml"),
     record(tool = "k8s_get_pod_logs"),
     record(tool = "k8s_get_events"),
     record(tool = "k8s_get_available_api_resources"),
     record(tool = "k8s_get_cluster_configuration"),
     record(tool = "k8s_check_service_connectivity"),
     record(tool = "k8s_apply_manifest"),
     record(tool = "k8s_patch_resource"),
     record(tool = "k8s_scale"),
     record(tool = "k8s_rollout"),
     record(tool = "k8s_label_resource"),
     record(tool = "k8s_annotate_resource"),
     record(tool = "k8s_execute_command")
| lookup [
    fetch spans
    | filter workshop.attendee == "${WORKSHOP_PREFIX}" and service.namespace == "kagent"
        and service.name == "${WORKSHOP_PREFIX}-sre-agent"
        and gen_ai.operation.name == "execute_tool"
        and gen_ai.tool.name != "(merged tools)"
    | summarize calls = count(), by:{tool = gen_ai.tool.name}
  ], sourceField:tool, lookupField:tool, prefix:"called_"
| fieldsAdd calls = coalesce(called_calls, 0)
| fieldsAdd verdict = if(calls == 0, "NEVER CALLED — drop candidate", else: "used")
| fieldsRemove called_tool, called_calls
| sort calls asc

sections.title: Granted vs. called tools (SRE agent) — drop the zero-call rows

sections.markdown:
## 4 · The change — trim the unused tools
In `agents/sre/sre-agent.yaml` the SRE agent grants **15 tools** from the built-in `kagent-tool-server`: 8 read/investigate tools plus 7 operate/write tools (`k8s_apply_manifest`, `k8s_patch_resource`, `k8s_scale`, `k8s_rollout`, `k8s_label_resource`, `k8s_annotate_resource`, `k8s_execute_command`). Every one of those schemas is injected into *every* prompt and billed as input tokens whether it is called or not. Section 3 shows that on an investigation workload the agent only ever fires a handful of the read tools — the write tools never run.

Trim `toolNames` down to just the tools the traces prove it uses, re-apply (`bash agents/install-agents.sh`), then re-run the **same** prompts so the before/after is apples-to-apples:

```yaml
- type: McpServer
  mcpServer:
    apiGroup: kagent.dev
    kind: RemoteMCPServer
    name: kagent-tool-server
    toolNames:          # was: 15 tools → now: only the read tools the traces show
      - k8s_get_resources
      - k8s_describe_resource
      - k8s_get_resource_yaml
      - k8s_get_pod_logs
      - k8s_get_events
      - k8s_check_service_connectivity
```

> Change **one** thing at a time. If you trim tools *and* shorten the prompt in the same step, you can't attribute the win.
> This trim is scoped to the **investigation** scenario. Re-grant the operate/write tools before you run a remediation demo — the agent can't `k8s_scale` or `k8s_rollout` what you took away.

## 5 · Re-measure — the before/after
The metric that moves is **avg input tokens per LLM call**, broken out **per agent**. Run this query over your **before** window, apply the change, replay the prompts, then run it again over the **after** window — reading the row for the agent you changed. The `timeframe` picker on this section is how you switch windows.

input.value:
fetch spans
| filter workshop.attendee == "${WORKSHOP_PREFIX}" and service.namespace == "kagent" and isNotNull(gen_ai.usage.input_tokens)
| summarize llmCalls = count(),
    avgInputPerCall = round(avg(gen_ai.usage.input_tokens)),
    medianInputPerCall = round(median(gen_ai.usage.input_tokens)),
    totalInputTokens = sum(gen_ai.usage.input_tokens), by:{service.name}
| sort avgInputPerCall desc

sections.title: Avg input tokens per call, by agent (switch the timeframe for before vs after)
Input-token trend by agent — watch the top line bend down after the change

sections.markdown:
## 6 · The rule — keep or revert
Ship the change only when **cost went down AND the eval pass rate did not** (module 05, `evals/dt-evals`). A cheaper agent that answers wrong is more expensive than the costly one that's right.

| Metric | Before | After | Keep? |
|---|:--:|:--:|:--:|
| Avg input tokens / call | _(§5)_ | _(§5)_ | — |
| Eval pass rate | _(module 05)_ | _(module 05)_ | ✅ only if ≥ before |

Then make it continuous: keep `dt-evals` in CI as a budget + regression gate, and alert when any agent's tokens-per-task drifts back up (companion dashboard: *Workshop · AI Agent Optimization*).
